issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, a transmission warning, or the car stuck in one gear.
issues.why: Premature automatic transmission failure is the most reported S-Type problem, usually showing up past about 100,000 miles. Early cars used a Ford-built five-speed and 2003-on cars a ZF six-speed; both have documented faults.
issues.next: Check the fluid and have the codes read by a shop that knows Jaguars. Some faults are fixed with software, a valve body or a solenoid instead of a full replacement.

issues.t: Timing chain tensioner failure
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine at cold start, rough running, or a sudden loss of power.
issues.why: Early 4.0L V8s used plastic timing chain tensioners and guides that go brittle and crack. If a chain jumps teeth, pistons can hit valves and wreck the engine. Jaguar switched to metal-reinforced and later all-metal parts.
issues.next: If you hear a rattle at start-up, shut the engine off and have it towed. If you don't know whether the tensioners were upgraded, have them inspected and replaced before they fail.

issues.t: Erratic or harsh shifts from valve body or solenoid
issues.sym: Hard or jerky shifts, flaring between gears, and a check engine light.
issues.why: On 2000-2002 cars a failed valve body or shift control solenoid upsets shift quality. Jaguar released a valve body kit.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read. A valve body or solenoid repair is much cheaper than a new gearbox if caught early.

issues.t: Torque converter lock-up fault
issues.sym: A check engine light with a torque converter code, higher revs at highway speed and worse fuel economy, or a shudder.
issues.why: Bulletins describe a missing oil seal on 2000-2002 cars and a faulty converter clutch lining on 2003 cars that keep the converter from locking.
issues.next: Have the code read and the fluid checked. A shop can tell you whether a seal or the converter itself is needed.

issues.t: Shift lever stuck in Park
issues.sym: The shifter won't come out of Park, especially when parked on a slope.
issues.why: The manual control lever on the transmission could bind. Jaguar's fix was a new lever.
issues.next: Set the parking brake before shifting into Park on hills. Have the shift linkage and lever checked.

issues.t: Low compression from worn Nikasil cylinder lining
issues.sym: Hard starting or no start, rough running and low compression.
issues.why: Early 4.0L V8s had Nikasil-coated cylinders that sulfur in US gasoline could wear away. Jaguar moved to steel liners in August 2000.
issues.next: Have a compression or leak-down test done. Damaged engines usually need a replacement short block.

issues.t: Misfire or no-start from water in spark plug wells
issues.sym: Misfires or a no-start after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water could get past the coil covers into the plug wells on 2000 V8 cars. Jaguar released a stiffer cover.
issues.next: Have the plug wells dried and the coils checked, and fit the updated covers.

issues.t: Misfire from failed ignition coil
issues.sym: Shaking at idle, loss of power and a check engine light.
issues.why: The coil-on-plug ignition coils fail often on the S-Type. On the V6, worn plugs and coils can also set camshaft sensor codes.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to find the cylinder. Replace the bad coil and check the spark plugs at the same time.

issues.t: Thermostat failure and false low-coolant warnings
issues.sym: The check engine light and low coolant warning come on, or the engine runs too cool or too hot.
issues.why: The 4.0L V8 thermostat wears out, and the coolant level sensor could give false readings when the coolant was dirty. Thermostats are a commonly replaced S-Type part.
issues.next: Check the coolant level with the engine cold. Have the thermostat tested and replaced if needed.

issues.t: Coolant pump outlet hose bursting
issues.sym: Sudden coolant loss, steam from the engine bay, and the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: Some 2004-2005 V6 cars got an outlet hose of the wrong specification that can split.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. Have the hose checked and replaced with the updated part.

issues.t: Check engine light from wet knock sensor
issues.sym: A check engine light with a knock sensor code.
issues.why: Water could drip through a hole in the cowl panel onto the knock sensor on some V6 cars.
issues.next: Have the sensor and wiring checked and the cowl hole sealed.

issues.t: Loss of power from failed fuel delivery hose
issues.sym: Power loss, hesitation or stalling, and possible fuel smell.
issues.why: On early 2000 cars some fuel additives broke down the fuel delivery hose, lowering fuel pressure. Later cars used a different hose material.
issues.next: Have the fuel pressure tested and hoses inspected. Any fuel smell is a fire risk, so get it checked right away.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Long cranking, sputtering at speed, or a no-start.
issues.why: The fuel pump is among the most replaced parts reported by S-Type owners.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: Transmission may select reverse while moving forward (recall)
issues.sym: The car could unexpectedly select reverse without warning.
issues.why: Low oil pressure or a sticking valve in the transmission. Jaguar recalled 2003 S-Types (NHTSA 04V024) to reprogram the transmission computer.
issues.next: Check with a Jaguar dealer that the recall update was done on your VIN.

issues.t: Electronic parking brake applying on its own (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake could switch on by itself while driving, locking the rear wheels.
issues.why: A fault in the electronic parking brake module. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 04V488) to replace the module.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was completed. If the brake ever applies unexpectedly, stop safely and have the car towed.

issues.t: Electronic parking brake won't release
issues.sym: The parking brake stays on and the car won't drive away, often with a warning message.
issues.why: The electronic parking brake won't release if battery voltage drops below about 8 volts, so a weak battery or loose battery cable can trap it.
issues.next: Check and charge the battery and clean the terminals. If the battery is fine, have the brake module diagnosed.

issues.t: Transmission may not fully engage Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park but the car can still roll.
issues.why: A badly made parking pawl guide plate. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 05V503) to replace the plate.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake and confirm the recall has been done.

issues.t: Front lower ball joint nuts loosening (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end or vague steering; in the worst case the ball joint stud can break.
issues.why: The ball joint nuts may not have been tightened properly at the factory. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 00V359) to check torque or replace the joints.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to confirm the recall was done and have the ball joints inspected.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No obvious symptom; the buckle may fail in a crash.
issues.why: Some TRW buckle bases weren't heat-treated correctly. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 00V228) to inspect and replace buckles.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall is complete.

issues.t: Weak air conditioning
issues.sym: The A/C blows cool rather than cold.
issues.why: Jaguar found the A/C compressor control valve on V6 cars could degrade, and released a modified valve spring.
issues.next: Have the A/C system pressures checked and ask about the valve fix before replacing the compressor.

issues.t: Ticking behind dashboard from blend door actuators
issues.sym: A ticking or bubbling noise from behind the dash, and temperature or airflow not doing what you set.
issues.why: The climate control blend door actuators give bad position feedback. Jaguar's fix was to replace all four.
issues.next: Have the climate system diagnosed. Replacing the actuators usually stops the noise.

issues.t: False warning lights and gauges dropping to zero
issues.sym: Warning lights come on for no reason, the fuel gauge reads empty, or the speedometer drops to zero.
issues.why: Instrument cluster software on 2003 cars. A battery disconnect only helps for a while; Jaguar released new cluster software.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or specialist to check the cluster software level.

issues.t: Key fob stops working
issues.sym: The remote won't lock or unlock the car, even with a new battery.
issues.why: Static build-up could damage the fob's microchip. Jaguar added an anti-static pad.
issues.next: Use the key in the door for now and have the fob checked or replaced and programmed.

issues.t: Front clunk from sway bar bushings or control arms
issues.sym: A thump or clunk from the front end over bumps, or inner-edge tire wear.
issues.why: Front stabilizer bar bushings wore on early cars, and control arms are among the most replaced S-Type parts.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected and get an alignment after any parts are replaced.

issues.t: Power steering squeal
issues.sym: A squeal when turning the steering wheel, especially at low speed.
issues.why: A seal inside the steering rack. Jaguar's fix was to replace part of the fluid with a special additive.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and ask a shop about the additive procedure.

issues.t: Thump from rear differential
issues.sym: A thump from the rear when pulling away or changing gear.
issues.why: The rear subframe mount bushings let the differential move. Jaguar added restrictor inserts.
issues.next: Have the rear subframe bushings inspected.

issues.t: Water in rear footwells
issues.sym: Wet carpet in the back, a musty smell or fogged windows.
issues.why: Water tracks in through the rear door latch area and gets trapped by the door seal. Later cars got a drain hole.
issues.next: Have the doors checked for the drain fix and dry the carpets fully.

issues.t: Limp mode or supercharger belt noise on S-Type R
issues.sym: A noisy belt after a cold start, or the car dropping into limp mode with a check engine light.
issues.why: Bulletins describe a supercharger drive belt that needed a revised design and water getting into the throttle position sensor housing.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the throttle sensor checked for water. Replace the belt with the updated part if it is noisy.

issues.t: Harsh shifts or chirping from six-speed automatic
issues.sym: Harsh 1-2 or downshifts, a chirp or squawk while shifting, or judder.
issues.why: Bulletins cover drifting adaptive shift settings and a sticking clutch inside the six-speed. Jaguar released software updates and a fluid additive.
issues.next: Have the transmission adaptations reset and software updated before considering bigger repairs.

issues.t: Can't shift out of gear from loose selector cable bracket
issues.sym: The shifter won't move properly or the gear shown doesn't match, and the engine may not start.
issues.why: The bolts holding the gear selector cable bracket can work loose.
issues.next: Have the selector cable and bracket checked and tightened or replaced.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak at wiring connector sleeve
issues.sym: Transmission fluid dripping near the side of the gearbox, sometimes with shift problems.
issues.why: The sleeve where the wiring connector passes into the transmission is a known leak point and is among parts owners report replacing.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and the sleeve replaced. Check the fluid level, because running low damages the transmission.

issues.t: Brakes and rotors wearing out early
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing and pads or rotors worn out well before 30,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners of 2007 cars report short brake life.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors measured and replace them as a set.
